answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable bond and prove control of a distinct verified device before it can trade. Like a raven returning to only one nest, an identity is bound to one attestation, so creating many fake agents means buying many devices and locking many bonds. A shared meadow of auditors can then spot clusters: if dozens of accounts share a funding source or plume of identical behavior, their bonds are frozen and slashed. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay linearly per fake identity, while an honest agent pays once, making large fake swarms unprofitable.
